content:
jess-support: FYI escalation from ACME — started ~09:12 UTC, seeing lots of 429s and long tail latency after a traffic spike. Customer says most requests are tiny (few tokens) and bursty. Pasting a short log sample and a curl we used to repro.

jess-support: ```
[2026-03-17T09:12:02Z] tenant=acme req_id=lkj123 status=429 model=redwood-1 seq=32 runtime_ms=1200 reason=quota_exhausted
[2026-03-17T09:12:02Z] tenant=acme req_id=lkj124 status=200 model=redwood-1 seq=8 runtime_ms=420 kv_cache=miss
[2026-03-17T09:12:03Z] tenant=acme req_id=lkj126 status=429 model=redwood-1 seq=12 runtime_ms=980 reason=quota_exhausted
```

jess-support: curl we used:```
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer xxxxx" -H "X-Redwood-Tenant: acme" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-1","input":"short prompt"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```

liam-sre: @jess-support thanks. quick q: is this a single region and single model? any spike in small concurrency vs sustained QPS? :eyes:

jess-support: single region EU-west, single model. Customer traffic ramped from ~20rps to ~250rps in ~30s. Many requests are < 50 tokens. They said client is chatty (one API call per UI keystroke).

ops-bot: ALERT: tenant=acme quota_burst_exceeded at 2026-03-17T09:12:02Z (threshold 200rps)

evan-eng: quick hypothesis: continuous batching + kv cache miss pattern -> lots of tiny batches with low aggregation efficiency, plus KV cache misses cause more work per request. The scheduler then enforces per-tenant flow-control -> 429s. Essentially perceived throttling even though node-level capacity still has headroom.

evan-eng: two immediate checks:
1) per-tenant concurrent inflight metric: `tenant.acme.inflight`
2) batch sizes/time-window distribution: `serving.batch.size_histogram{tenant=acme}`

evan-eng: also grep trace logs for `kv_cache=miss` correlated with `batch_size<=3`. If you see a lot of misses on tiny batches, that explains the sawtooth pattern.

jess-support: I pulled the metrics: inflight spiked to 180, median batch size dropped to 2, kv_cache miss rate jumped to 68% during the peak.

liam-sre: ok repro looks solid. Short-term mitigation options:
- flip on per-tenant smoothing to allow short burst absorb (config: `tenant_rate.limit.burst_window_ms = 1000`)
- increase per-tenant burst quota for ACME temporarily
- enable server-side small-request aggregation (experimental) which delays dispatch by +30ms to increase batch size

mika-product: for customer comms, can we give a simple action they can take client-side? they asked for something to do now.

evan-eng: client-side: debounce keystroke calls (batch inputs) or coalesce small prompts into a single call. Server-side: set `batch.window_ms` from 20 -> 50 and enable `kv_cache.warmup=true` for tenant. Example config snippet:```
{
  "tenants": {
    "acme": {
      "rate": {"burst_quota": 400, "burst_window_ms": 1000},
      "batching": {"window_ms": 50, "max_batch_size": 128},
      "kv_cache": {"warmup": true, "warmup_tokens": 256}
    }
  }
}
```

liam-sre: diagnostic command for traces:```
rdwctl traces query --tenant=acme --from=2026-03-17T09:10:00Z --to=2026-03-17T09:15:00Z --filter "kv_cache=miss" --group-by batch_size
```

evan-eng: repro script (small loop to simulate):```
for i in `seq 1 300`; do \
  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer x" -H "X-Redwood-Tenant: acme" \
    -d '{"model":"redwood-1","input":"a"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate &
  sleep 0.05
done
```

jess-support: I applied the temporary burst_quota bump and enabled batching.window_ms=50 for tenant acme. Ops alert cleared after ~40s, 429s dropped to near zero, tail latency improved. Customer will debounce on client side as well. :thumbsup:

mika-product: great — can we document recommended defaults for chatty clients and put a short KB on debounce + server flags? I'll draft.

liam-sre: followups: open ticket to evaluate small-request-aggregation GA; add a knob in console to toggle tenant-level warmup. Also log a postmortem note with metrics.

jess-support: filing follow-ups now. Thanks team. :raised_hands:
